provider.notes: Yandex SpeechKit. The vendor streams only over gRPC (v3 recommended, v2 legacy; no WebSocket) and the gateway has no gRPC client for it, so every model that can serve a call needs the file-upload transport. The client registered today (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs) is a synchronous REST client behind a 500 ms wall-clock timer. It is not a transport: when_unusable on each row records what a live session gets from it, and decisions section 5 keeps it, reported as known broken, until the file-upload transport is enabled. It is billed one 15 s unit for each half-second piece and ends a turn on every piece, so keeping it is costly and unusable for conversation. Aliases: the standardized factory accepts yandex, yandex-speechkit, yandex_speechkit and speechkit (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:471); the plugin registry also accepts yandex-stt and yandex_stt (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1744-1746), which today miss the standardized path. Gateway-side model aliases (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:187-201) are not wire strings: 'default' is a model_aliases entry of the general row, and 'rc' and 'realtime' of the general:rc row. 'batch' means the gateway's own id 'deferred' and has no alias entry (an alias cannot sit on the 'deferred*' pattern row), so the resolver must still rewrite it to 'deferred' before lookup; otherwise it falls to the provider default row and would be sent to the vendor as the 'topic' value. Today's client replaces any id it does not know with 'general' (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:291-295). The API host uses a publicly trusted certificate chain, unlike Sber and T-Bank.

transports.disabled_reason: The per-utterance file-upload adapter (segmented_yandex) is not implemented. The Yandex client registered today is not a substitute: it uploads whatever audio accumulated about every 500 ms on a wall-clock timer, speech or silence, and marks each piece as the end of a turn (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:219-332). Enable once the adapter ships and one live call has passed.

rates.note: Synchronous recognition requests. Whether the quota is per folder or per cloud is not stated.

gateway_client.notes: The request and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /speech/v1/stt:recognize) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: send headerless PCM16, not WAV (the vendor accepts only LPCM without a WAV header, or OggOpus); send sampleRateHertz equal to the upload rate as well as format=lpcm (the vendor default is 48000 and only 8000, 16000 and 48000 are accepted); keep every upload under 30 s and 1 MB including pre-roll and trailing silence (the legacy overflow cap of 1,024,000 bytes at client.rs:37 is 32 s at 16 kHz); never upload a segment without speech, because an empty request is billed one 15 s unit; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 0.95 (client.rs:293-297). limits.rates records the vendor quota of 20 synchronous requests per second in the vendor's own window; the limiter must hold the per-second rate. An HTTP 429 currently counts as a failure on the breaker shared by every Yandex session (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:137-140).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 8000 ms in total, with about 2 s to connect, is the vendor audit's provisional value, not a measurement: Yandex publishes no latency for the synchronous endpoint, and the legacy client allows 60 s with no connect timeout (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:22-26). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit the vendor limits: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB at 16 kHz, inside 30 s and 1 MB; the adapter should still refuse to send more than 29 s, and must never upload 48 kHz PCM, where 1 MB holds about 10.9 s. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause).

gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/messages.rs:33-42 (unused placeholder types); gateway/Cargo.toml:282 (tonic 0.11 already a dependency)
gateway_client.notes: Vendor endpointing through the default end-of-utterance classifier (sensitivity DEFAULT or HIGH, with a pause hint). The vendor sends a final result only when an end-of-utterance event fires. Session rules a client must respect: at most 5 minutes and 10 MB of audio per session, one channel, and the session is closed after 5 s without a message, so the client needs silence_chunk keep-alives and a rollover before the limit. The name of the language field in the gRPC v3 request is not in the evidence: dialect.language_param records 'language_code', the name used by the gateway's unused placeholder type (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/messages.rs:41-43), and it must be confirmed against the v3 proto before a client is built. limits.rates records the vendor quota of 40 streaming requests per second. Billing starts when the settings message is sent.

gateway_client.notes: Same RPC as stream_yandex, opened with the ExternalEouClassifier option ('Use EOU provided by user' in the v3 proto) instead of the default classifier. billing.notes: An empty request is billed one 15 s unit. Streaming is billed by the same rule from the moment the settings message is sent. No pricing key exists for this provider in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs.

rates.note: Synchronous recognition requests. Whether the quota is per folder or per cloud is not stated.

gateway_client.notes: The request and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /speech/v1/stt:recognize) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: send headerless PCM16, not WAV (the vendor accepts only LPCM without a WAV header, or OggOpus); send sampleRateHertz equal to the upload rate as well as format=lpcm (the vendor default is 48000 and only 8000, 16000 and 48000 are accepted); keep every upload under 30 s and 1 MB including pre-roll and trailing silence (the legacy overflow cap of 1,024,000 bytes at client.rs:37 is 32 s at 16 kHz); never upload a segment without speech, because an empty request is billed one 15 s unit; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 0.95 (client.rs:293-297). limits.rates records the vendor quota of 20 synchronous requests per second in the vendor's own window; the limiter must hold the per-second rate. An HTTP 429 currently counts as a failure on the breaker shared by every Yandex session (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:137-140).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 8000 ms in total, with about 2 s to connect, is the vendor audit's provisional value, not a measurement: Yandex publishes no latency for the synchronous endpoint, and the legacy client allows 60 s with no connect timeout (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:22-26). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit the vendor limits: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB at 16 kHz, inside 30 s and 1 MB; the adapter should still refuse to send more than 29 s, and must never upload 48 kHz PCM, where 1 MB holds about 10.9 s. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause).

when_unusable.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:219-332 (500 ms timer uploads); gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:291-295 (an id the parser does not know is sent as general)

billing.notes: An empty request is billed one 15 s unit. Streaming is billed by the same rule from the moment the settings message is sent. No pricing key exists for this provider in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs.

provenance.notes: Fail-slow default for a Yandex model id the map does not know: file upload to the synchronous endpoint with the id passed as 'topic'. A wrong guess fails with a vendor error on the first segment instead of at session setup. Today the gateway silently replaces any unknown id with 'general' (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:291-295); the plan should replace that with strict parsing. The gateway's own aliases default, rc and realtime are model_aliases of the general and general:rc rows; 'batch' has no alias entry and must still be rewritten to 'deferred' before lookup, so that it does not land on this row and reach the vendor as a 'topic' value.
